title: Pleasant to people (Avot 3:10)
hookLine: whoever is pleasing to people is pleasing to God
tomorrow: where does a whole day go?

cards: Opening night, five o'clock, and somebody's already snapped at the kid running the lights. Can being liked by people mean anything to God? Chanina ben Dosa says it does.
In Avot: whoever the spirit of people is at ease with, the spirit of God is at ease with. And whoever the spirit of people isn't at ease with, neither is the spirit of God.
The way people breathe around you, he says, is a clue to how heaven does.

teach.b: Start with the word he uses for people: briyot, creatures. Not one group, not the people who agree with you; everyone God made. Hillel uses the same word back in chapter one, loving the creatures.
So the measure is wide. The lighting kid counts. The stranger at the counter counts.
Second, the word for pleased is nochah, at ease, settled. It isn't about being popular, or agreeing with everyone so nobody's ever upset.
It's whether people can rest around you: whether your presence makes a room easier or harder to breathe in. Third, the life version. A hard week, a short temper, an apology that's late but real.
Being pleasant to people is a practice, not a personality; it's built one interaction at a time, often right after you've blown one. Fourth, the hard edge.

teach.h: CHECKED BY THE PEOPLE AROUND YOU.
teach.b: It's a demanding test, because it's checked by the people around you, not by your own opinion of yourself.
Chanina ben Dosa puts God's ease and people's ease side by side, so how someone treats the creatures can't be separated from how they stand with the Creator.

how: Jewish ethical teaching, from Avot to the Mussar tradition, treats pleasant, respectful dealing with every person as part of serving God, not separate from it.

o: flattering people so they think well of you
being someone everyone can be at ease around
keeping quiet so you never upset anyone

games.q: the words inside the saying — tap the pairs.

s: the Hebrew word for people here, briyot, means creatures
everyone God made, not one group.
Avot 3:10 means please everyone, whatever it takes
the word is at ease: whether people can rest around you, not whether you flatter them.
being pleasant to people is separate from how one stands with God
Chanina ben Dosa puts the two side by side.

games.q: a coworker says being pleasant to everyone is fake; she'd rather be blunt and honest. what does Avot 3:10 point to?
o: honest, and still someone people can be at ease around.
agree with everyone so nobody is ever upset.
blunt is better, since God cares only about the truth.
games.why: the saying's word is at ease. honesty can stay; the test is whether people can rest around you.

practice: Let your face soften, jaw, forehead, the skin around your eyes, the way it does when someone you're glad to see walks in. Hold that ease through a few slow breaths.
Then bring to mind one person you've been short with lately, and keep the softness while you think of them.

wordCard.voice: Pleasant to people: when the spirit of people is at ease with someone, Chanina ben Dosa says, so is the spirit of God.

orig.note: Hebrew: the spirit of people is at ease with him, Avot 3:10.

carryVoice: Your line: pleasant to people. Everyone counts, starting with whoever happens to be nearest. See you tomorrow.

sources.ref: Mishnah, Pirkei Avot 3:10 (Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa: the spirit of people and the spirit of God)
Mishnah, Pirkei Avot 1:12 (Hillel: loving the creatures)
